newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls to 11.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls to 11.1 percent.

text.p: Croatia's money market rate tumbled 70 basis points to 11.1 percent, as high supply of kuna funds overshot demand by almost eight times.
Banks sought only 8.5 million kuna ($1.5 million) in fresh loans and another 9.5 million were rolled over. Daily trade left a surplus of 122 million on the supply side.
Insurers cut the rate for one-week funds to 9.0 percent from 10. Banks charged between 13 and 17 percent for term loans.
The weighted call money rate was steady at 10.5 percent.

The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday firmer at 5.8867 against the dollar and at 3.5623 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 5.853 Croatian Kuna)
